Anderson\n\nDocket Number: 59-60\n\nDate of Argument: October 1, 2021\n\nDate of Decision: June 20, 2022\n\nQuestion Presented: Whether former President Donald J. Trump is ineligible for future federal office under Section 3 of the Fourteenth Amendment due to his role in the January 6, 2021, Capitol insurrection.\n\nMajority Opinion (written by Chief Justice John Roberts, joined by Justices Breyer, Sotomayor, and Kagan):\n\nThe Court holds that former President Donald J. Trump is not ineligible for future federal office under Section 3 of the Fourteenth Amendment. While the events of January 6, 2021, were a grave assault on our democratic institutions, the language of the Fourteenth Amendment requires a formal determination of insurrection or rebellion by Congress or a court of competent jurisdiction. In this case, no such determination has been made. The Court acknowledges the serious concerns raised by the petitioner but emphasizes the importance of adhering to the Constitution's text and structure. The political process, not the judiciary, is the appropriate avenue for addressing the fitness of a candidate for federal office.\n\nConcurring Opinion (written by Justice Brett Kavanaugh, joined by Justice Amy Coney Barrett):\n\nWhile I agree with the majority's conclusion, I write separately to emphasize that the Constitution's text and history support a narrow interpretation of Section 3 of the Fourteenth Amendment. The provision was intended to address the specific circumstances of the post-Civil War era and should not be expansively applied to modern political disputes. The political branches have the primary responsibility for determining the qualifications of candidates for federal office, and the judiciary should be reluctant to intervene in such matters.\n\nDissenting Opinion (written by Justice Neil Gorsuch, joined by Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito):\n\nThe majority's decision today undermines the very purpose of Section 3 of the Fourteenth Amendment. The provision was designed to protect our democratic institutions from those who would seek to overthrow them.
